arc-b.best: The type does the before/after: heavy grotesk 'Good ideas die' over italic serif 'in bad first lines', and a lime highlighter on the sharpened line. It's the most arresting first frame of the ten, and the receipts, the sunset 11 PM to 8:40 AM band and the lime CTA carry it to the footer.
arc-b.worst: Too much going on: two stickers ('Free, unlimited', 'Your facts stay'), two handwritten notes with arrows, tape, five pastel tile colours. Grotesk tracking is so tight the letters in 'ideas' touch. Ultramarine is gone entirely. ~300KB of base64 fonts inlined (Bricolage, Instrument Serif) instead of ../../fonts or a Google Fonts link. The edit is already done at 300ms, so the tap itself is never shown.
arc-b.hero1s_adjust: +0.4: poster-grade contrast (black grotesk, italic serif, lime band) lands in under a second at both 1440 and 390

arc-a.best: Stays inside the brand and still hits: a full-bleed ultramarine stage, a dark composer with amber stickers on 'so i think the' and 'is honestly just', a heycape cursor that taps Sharpen, and the stickers peel off into a tray. The final CTA brings the stickers back, which ties the page together.
arc-a.worst: Below the hero it drops back to standard dark-SaaS bento (one blue tile), so the sticker idea never comes back until the footer CTA. The receipt sits under the fold at 1440x900, and mid-animation frames clip first letters ('ost underrated…' on phone).
arc-a.hero1s_adjust: +0.3: blue field plus amber chips on the soft words read as 'something is wrong with this line' at 300ms

awwwards-b.best: The most ownable idea in the round. Brand blue becomes the editor's blue pencil, and proofreader's marks (strike, caret, cap, move loop) draw themselves on a taped galley proof, with a real pencil object and margin notes. It holds from hero to pricing (the $12 is circled in pencil).
awwwards-b.worst: Legibility drops wherever the idea is busiest. The churn proof's marks collide ('What changed:' over '34%'), the draft is small Geist Mono, there are four faces (Garamond, Mono, Caveat, Inter), and the nav and labels are tiny uppercase mono. Uppercase kickers sit above the persona h3s, which bends the no-eyebrow rule. The bottom ~20% of the 1440x900 hero is empty.
awwwards-b.hero1s_adjust: 0: 'Post it sharp.' is big and the proof reads as 'editing', but at 1s the marks are only half-drawn

apple-b.best: Loudest in-brand-colour hero: a full ultramarine field, huge Inter Display 'Write the line / they stop for.', one crisp white post sitting still in a drifting blurred feed of soft openers. Good section rhythm (blue, paper, black) and the '309 / 280' thread-split moment.
apple-b.worst: The hero shows the result, not the edit. The card is static, the strike-through is a hairline, and nothing sharpens in front of you. Bold Inter on blue reads like a well-made template, not Hookworthy, and the serif voice is gone. Blue appears in at least four places, not the 'three' claimed.
apple-b.hero1s_adjust: +0.2: instant colour and scale, held back because the product's one move never happens on screen

typefully-b.best: The receipt idea runs the whole page: a thermal receipt prints down from the nav rule, the 11:04 PM to Friday timetable replaces the feature grid, and pricing is set as receipts. The closing 'Your next post starts here.' input underlines soft words live as you type, and it's honest about what runs in the app.
typefully-b.worst: At 300ms the hero is a serif headline on beige with a sliver of receipt. Printing finishes at ~2s, and the receipt is a narrow low-contrast mono column you can't read at a glance. On phone the receipt is below the fold. 'MARKETS'-style small-caps labels on the persona cards come close to the kicker ban.
typefully-b.hero1s_adjust: -0.2: the first second is typography only; the signature (the print) arrives late and small

linear-b.best: The best punchline of the round, 'Your idea is fine. / Your first line isn't.', plus a hook drawn as an engineered part: hairline stage, crosshairs, and leader-line callouts ('CUT · The warm-up', 'MOVE · Asked it as a question', 'KEPT · Your facts'). The pricing comparison table is the clearest of the ten.
linear-b.worst: Near-black and bone with no ultramarine, and almost no motion (frames are pixel-identical from 1s to 6s). The labels are 11-12px mono and the hover is desktop-only. It's very refined, and very likely to get the same 'plain' reaction from the founder again.
linear-b.hero1s_adjust: -0.2: the diagram is smart but colourless; the eye lands on a small struck line before the big headline

awwwards-a.best: The cut words fall onto a 'cutting floor' you can poke, and each pile word shows on hover why it was cut. Every feature title is sharpened with the generic SaaS line struck through underneath, which is the best content device on any of the pages.
awwwards-a.worst: The edit fires too early and stutters. The 1s frame shows overlapping words ('Sizing' over 'down') mid-FLIP, and the floor is already piled at 300ms, so the fall is never seen. The pile reads as clutter at the bottom of the hero. Mid-page has dead voids (the 'Replies don't pay' block is half empty), and the caption 'The cutting floor. Poke it.' is ~10px.
awwwards-a.hero1s_adjust: -0.1: the headline is huge and asymmetric with a blue full stop, but the first second shows a janky in-between frame

typefully-a.best: 'They read one line. / Make it *hookworthy*.' has a nice blue rule under the italic, and 'See the squiggle? Tap Sharpen.' has a real try-it textarea that flags soft words live and honestly says the rewrite runs in the app.
typefully-a.worst: It looks a lot like the current dark site. The hero is a crowded stack of three cards with the receipt cut by the fold at 1440x900, and the sticky feature index is a familiar pattern. Network counters fail AA (4.33:1 at 11.5px).
typefully-a.hero1s_adjust: -0.2: a good headline, but the visual is a busy pile of dark cards that arrive in sequence

linear-a.best: Tight product craft: a real composer with sidebar, word-level strike-through, a green receipt '90 → 59', a live X preview, Sharpen ⌘↵ undo and replay, and a tilt that flattens on scroll. The best keyboard and a11y hygiene in the round (skip link, focus rings).
linear-a.worst: A centred headline over an app screenshot in a frame is the Typefully and SaaS-template structure the founder ruled out, on the same dark Newsreader look that was called plain. The edit is small inside a big UI frame.
linear-a.hero1s_adjust: -0.3: the first second reads as 'another dark SaaS with a screenshot'

apple-a.best: A disciplined two-tone heading system ('Same idea.' dim / 'Sharper line.' bright) used on every section. A pause control on the cycling demo, and the giant struck 'Auto-DMs / Auto-replies / Auto-deletes / Auto-reposts' stack is a strong trust moment.
apple-a.worst: Calm, centred and dark, which is exactly the 'plain' the founder complained about. The rewrite is set in Inter at UI size inside a big empty card, so the hero looks like a settings panel. The page is long and sections repeat the same centred stack.
apple-a.hero1s_adjust: -0.3: nothing at 1s pulls you in; the sharpen lands at ~2s and is quiet

top5.why: The only concept where the first frame feels like a poster, not a SaaS page. The grotesk/italic split is the before/after made into type, and the lime highlight on 'Most underrated thing in trading? Sizing down after a loss.' is the punchline. The receipt system (proof card, till receipt, four tilted receipt cards, pricing) keeps it consistent while staying loud, and it is nothing like Typefully.

The strongest result inside the current brand: ultramarine finally used as a stage, not a button, with tactile amber stickers that peel off the soft words when heycape taps Sharpen. It answers 'plain' without throwing away Newsreader and blue, and the sticker callback in the final CTA closes the loop. Held back only by a generic dark-bento middle.

The most original and ownable idea: the blue pencil. Proofreader's marks drawing over a taped galley proof explain Sharpen better than any UI screenshot, and the art direction (tape, pencil, circled $12, 'SENT BY YOU' stamp) holds the whole way down. It needs legibility discipline to compete on impact.

The fastest one-second hit after arc-b: full ultramarine field, huge two-line Inter Display, one crisp post in a drifting blurred feed. The alternating blue/paper/black rhythm is confident and the copy is tight. It sells the outcome but never shows the move, and it trades the brand's serif voice for template-grade Inter.

The most complete idea system on paper: receipt hero, timetable in place of features, receipt pricing, and a live-squiggle input as the closer. Copy is excellent ('Every edit, on the record.'). The hero just whispers: its signature prints late and narrow, so the first second is only a headline.

steal: linear-b: the punchline 'Your idea is fine. / Your first line isn't.' (best line in the round). Use it as the hero sub-head or closing headline.
linear-b: leader-line anatomy labels (CUT · The warm-up / MOVE · Asked it as a question / KEPT · Your facts) as the visual grammar of the receipt, with chips on phone.
linear-b: the plan comparison table (Included / Not included rows) under the three price cards.
awwwards-a: sharpen every feature title and strike the generic SaaS version underneath (e.g. 'Four feeds. One draft.' over a struck 'we show you previews for every platform').
awwwards-a: the cutting floor as a page-end gag, where every soft word cut on the page piles up above the footer ('Everything cut on this page.'). Keep it out of the hero.
typefully-a: 'See the squiggle? Tap Sharpen.' as the how-it-works headline, plus the honest try-it textarea that flags soft words live and says the rewrite runs in the app.
apple-a: a pause button on any auto-cycling hero demo, and the giant struck 'Auto-DMs / Auto-replies / Auto-deletes / Auto-reposts' stack as the trust section.
linear-a: ⌘↵ / Undo on the hero demo so visitors can replay the edit, and the composer tilt that flattens on scroll.
apple-b: the '309 / 280 → becomes a thread of 2' moment for the previews section.
typefully-b (for whichever wins): the 11:04 PM → 8:40 AM → Friday timetable as the features section instead of a grid.
notes: Method: read all 10 rationales and the brief, viewed every supplied screenshot, then drove each page live in Playwright. I captured the hero at 0.3/1/2/3/4.5/6/9s (1440) and 1/3.5/7s (390 phone), measured frame-to-frame pixel change, ran each main interaction (example switchers, Next proof, Print another, Try yours / Try it here typing, Stick them back on, Monthly toggle), checked keyboard focus, and scanned every page at 1440/390/360 with reduced motion on. Hard-rule checks: no horizontal scroll at 360 or 390 on any concept. All h1/h2/h3 are at most two lines at 1440 and 390. Prices, including monthly toggles ($16 / $24), are correct everywhere. No banned words found. No gradient text. All reduced-motion states render complete. Violations and near-misses: arc-b inlines ~300KB of base64 fonts (Bricolage Grotesque, Instrument Serif) instead of ../../fonts or a Google Fonts link. awwwards-b has uppercase kicker labels above the persona h3s ('CRYPTO AND TRADING'), and typefully-b uses similar small-caps 'MARKETS' labels. Contrast misses: typefully-a counters at 4.33:1 (11.5px) and the awwwards-b X glyph at 2.79:1. Everything else passed AA in my scan. Motion is modest across the board: no concept animates the actual tap-to-sharpen inside the first second except arc-a (stickers visible at 0.3s, tap at ~2s) and awwwards-a (which fires too early and shows an overlapping-words frame at 1s). The founder's 'plain' complaint lines up with the dark -a variants (apple-a, linear-a, typefully-a). The three that clearly fix it are arc-b, arc-a and apple-b. Recommended direction: arc-b's type-as-before/after and receipt system, with ultramarine back as the single primary and arc-a's peel-off moment as the hero animation.
